newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean rebel suspect asks France for asylum.
newsitem.headline: Chilean rebel suspect asks France for asylum.

text.p: An accused Chilean left-wing guerrilla wanted on weapons charges holed himself up in the French Embassy on Friday, demanding asylum after a prosecutor issued an arrest warrant for him, Chilean officials said.

An alleged member of the Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front, Domiciano Alberto Soto, and his sister walked into the embassy and requested asylum, alleging they were victims of political persecution, deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco said.
It was not immediately known if the sister, Maria Antonia Soto, faced any charges or arrest warrants.
A military judge issued an arrest warrant for Soto on Monday on charges of smuggling weapons, and issued another order the next day barring him from leaving the country, said Velasco.

"I have made it clear to the ambassador that Soto has an arrest warrant out, issued by ... a military court," Velasco told reporters. "The ambassador told me he had informed Paris about what happened and that he was waiting for instructions."

Reporters saw a heavy police presence around the embassy in Santiago's posh Providencia neighbourhood since about midday on Friday. French officials, apparently eager to keep news of the asylum bid under wraps, for hours denied rumours that a fleeing guerrilla was inside until Velasco confirmed them.
The exact charges against Soto were not clear, and nor were his reasons for choosing France for his asylum request.

The Manuel Rodriguez group, named for a 19th-century rebel against Spanish colonial rule, scored its most famous blow in 1986 when it wounded military ruler Gen. Augusto Pinochet in an assassination attempt, in which five of Pinochet's bodyguards died.
The group, which has been thought to be dormant since the early 1990s, lept back to life in December when it rescued four of its leaders from jail in a daring helicopter raid.
Chilean police later said they had strong indications of help in the rescue from the Irish Republican Army and sent investigators to Ireland and Britain to check out leads.
